name: Tobanga
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Jungraithmayr 1977 subclassification comment on Glottolog; no grammar or phonology of Tobanga located online.

sources.citation: Seignobos, Christian. 1982. Matières grasses, parcs et civilisations agraires (Tchad et Nord-Cameroun). Cahiers d'outre-mer 35(139): 229-269.
sources.note: Ethnographic mention of the Tobanga people only (Persée hit); irrelevant to stress.

sources.citation: Bouny, Paule. 1978. La formation du pluriel des nominaux en kotoko (pp. 51-66) and Bouny & Jouannet, Comparaison lexicale kanembou-kotoko (p.180), same SELAF volume.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The accent rule ('un accent, qui ne peut frapper que la syllabe finale ou la pénultième') is stated for KOTOKO, not Tobanga -- checked because the archive.org snippet juxtaposed it with 'tobanga'.

sources.citation: Wolff, Ekkehard. 1983. Tonogenese in tschadischen Sprachen. Afrika und Übersee 66: (Tobanga passage pp. 212-213).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Second-hand from Caprile 1978:128: Tobanga marked with four tones (Hoch, Mittelhoch, Mitteltief, Tief), voiced-onset verbs carry lower tone patterns (depressor effect); speaks of 'Tobanga 4(!?)-Ton-System'. Nothing on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann (ed.). 1982. The Chad languages in the Hamitosemitic-Nigritic border area (Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde A 27). Berlin: Reimer. [sibine chapter citing Caprile 1978:147-150 on Tobanga verb classes]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Tobanga only for verb sub-classification criteria (incl. linear vs complex tone scheme) and complex consonant series; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Caprile, Jean-Pierre. 1978. Les mots voyageurs dans l'interfluve Bahr-Erguig/Chari/Logone: comparaison lexicale entre le barma.. et le tumak, langue tchadique. In J.-P. Caprile & H. Jungraithmayr (eds.), Préalables à la reconstruction du proto-tchadique, 145-156. Paris: SELAF. [p.149 fn.1 on Tobanga]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; footnote by the describer of Tobanga himself: 'le tobanga est une langue à quatre registres phonétiques. Le tréma indique le ton ponctuel le plus bas.' (p.149).

sources.citation: Caprile, Jean-Pierre. 1978. Notes linguistiques sur le tobanga à partir d'un conte en cette langue. In H. Jungraithmayr & J.-P. Caprile (eds.), Cinq textes tchadiques (Cameroun et Tchad): présentation linguistique (Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde, Serie A: Afrika), 121-175. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only linguistic sketch of Tobanga (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description, 55 pp.); contains the phonology with the four-tone analysis (p.128) -- the one place a statement on accent/stress (or its absence) would be.

sources.citation: Vanderkooi, Mark, William Chesley & Jean Doun. 1990. Rapport d'une enquête sociolinguistique entre le Gabri du Nord (Tobanga) et le Gabri du Sud (Dormo/Darbe). N'Djaména: SIL Tchad. 28 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other modern document on the language; SIL surveys occasionally include a phonology note and would point to any SIL Tchad phonology/orthography statement for Gabri-Nord.

sources.citation: [Reviewer n.n.] 1981. Review of Jungraithmayr & Caprile (eds.), Cinq textes tchadiques (1978). Orientalistische Literaturzeitung 76(2).
